data.narrative:
Nu Quantum, a Series A quantum computing company founded by Carmen Palacios-Berraquero, is evaluated against a sector comprising 3 public comps (IONQ, RGTI, QBTS) and 8 private peers including Quantinuum, IonQ, D-Wave Quantum, Rigetti Computing, and Infleqtion.

The valuation analysis applies a single triangulation method: stage-progression analysis. Using the company's $60M total raised as a valuation proxy, a 2.0x multiplier typical of Series A to next-stage advancement yields an implied valuation of $120M. The peer-median approach proved inapplicable due to insufficient narrow-filter peer data—while 5 same-sector peers exist, none of the same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier filters generated three or more comparable datapoints. A broader sector median would introduce material noise.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $102M to $138M, centered on $120M. This range reflects ±15% variance around the stage-progression implied value. Key uncertainties include the limited applicability of a single method and the absence of direct same-stage peer multiples in quantum computing—a sector where funding dynamics and investor appetite remain volatile. The valuation is most defensible as a stage-based floor rather than a market-derived estimate. Investors should treat this range as illustrative pending access to more granular peer multiples or transaction comparables.
